subject: Sierra evaluation readout & success rubric
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Lina Ortiz <lina.ortiz@sierra-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Sierra evaluation readout & success rubric

Hi Lina — great conversation this morning. Quick recap and proposed POC success rubric so we can align with your engineering and procurement teams.

Goals we heard from Sierra:
- Validate API-level latency and throughput at production scale for key intents
- Verify cost per inference with realistic call patterns
- Confirm output quality on your labeled test-set and edge cases

Proposed evaluation plan (4-week pilot):
1) Success criteria (pass/fail gates):
   - Latency: p95 <= 400 ms (single-threaded, 16k context typical workflow)
   - Throughput: sustained 50 requests/sec with 50 concurrent connections (burst to 100)
   - Cost: amortized cost/token <= $0.0004 (including packaging/round-trip overhead)
   - Quality: top-1 intent accuracy >= 92% on seed dataset; precision/recall thresholds by intent (we'll map once you provide labels)
2) Measurement & instrumentation:
   - Redwood will run a mixed workload harness using your sample traces; we’ll publish per-route token counts, p50/p95/p99 latency, and GPU util by shard.
   - You provide: canonical test corpus (CSV + labels), typical request size distribution, and a strawman traffic profile.
3) Ownership & ops:
   - Redwood owner (technical): me (Jonas) — overall trial lead and escalation contact
   - Implementation owner: Marissa Cole — onboarding, model selection, infra config
   - Commercial/SLA owner: Ben Carter — pricing, reserved capacity and any credits
   - Sierra owners: Lina (engineering) + procurement contact (procurement@sierra-analytics.com)
4) Timeline (proposed):
   - Kickoff & data handoff: 2026-11-28
   - Week 1: environment prep, baseline runs, and initial tuning
   - Week 2–3: steady-state runs, latency/throughput tuning, cached prefix experiments
   - Week 4: quality evaluation, final readout, and decision meeting (target completion 2026-12-26)
5) Risk/fallbacks:
   - If p95 target not met at required cost, Redwood proposes an alternative: lower-cost quantized model variant with slightly higher quality guardrails or a regional routing policy to reduce cross-region RTs.

Attachments: sierra-poc-matrix.xlsx (POC metric template), network-topology.png (sample connectivity notes). I’ll attach a draft quote after we confirm POC scope.

Next steps / asks for Sierra: please confirm the dataset deliverable and whether you need a private deployment (VPC) for test traffic. Also share the procurement contact so Ben can loop in pricing/contract cadence.

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
From: Lina Ortiz <lina.ortiz@sierra-analytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, procurement@sierra-analytics.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Sierra evaluation readout & success rubric

Jonas — thanks for the quick write-up and the clear plan. A few items from our side: we can meet most of this but need to tighten the latency target. On our internal SLAs, p95 <= 300 ms is what product teams expect for critical intents. Is that achievable without pushing cost above the $0.0004/token target?

We will provide:
- Labeled test set (approx. 12k examples) by EOD 2026-11-25
- Representative traffic traces and sample payload sizes
- Procurement contact here: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@sierra-analytics.com> (adding to the thread)

Also: we prefer Private (VPC) test traffic for the pilot due to data classification. Please highlight any extra lead time / infra prep and whether that changes the POC timeline.

On quality: we care most about intent recall for high-risk flows (fraud detection intents). We’ll mark those in the dataset. If you could propose per-intent thresholds (precision/recall) in the POC matrix that would help.

Appreciate it — Lina
Lina Ortiz | Head of Product Engineering
Sierra Analytics

- baseline p95 on hosted API with their expected median request size (I’ll share traces once we receive them)
- p95 with dedicated capacity (N GPUs) and with region-local routing
- p95 with quantized variant and cache enabled (KV prefix cache) and the cost delta per-token

Ben — flag any commercial implications if they require Private VPC for the pilot (we may need a short-term infra setup fee + longer lead time). If Private adds >5 business days, we’ll propose running week 1 on hosted with obfuscated samples while vpc is stood up.

Owner matrix (internal):
- Kickoff & infra provision: Marissa (action: estimate GPU footprint and lead time)
- Instrumentation & harness: Jonas (action: publish harness and testing template)
- Commercial/contract: Ben (action: draft POC quote and short term PS scoping)

I’ll draft the per-intent thresholds once we get the labeled set. Also, prepare a short set of fallback model variants (2 options) to present at kickoff so Sierra can choose trade-offs.

Jonas
